name: PT Indo Acidatama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indo Acidatama: the molasses margin holds and the harvest bill arrives
frontmatter.summary: The molasses spread held through the third quarter and nine-month net profit reached IDR100.2bn [S6]. We keep BUY with a target of Rp125, a 32.5% total return. The valuation rests on the cash flow alone: the trailing multiple legs are withdrawn because the data pack understated depreciation, and the bull now carries volume only, with no margin uplift that a filing supports.
thesis: The molasses spread is the value case: nine-month gross profit of IDR260.2bn on sales of IDR862.9bn is a margin earned on industrial, food-grade and export volumes where the regulated fuel formula does not set the price [S6, S3].

Volume, not price, is the growth lever. The plant runs near nameplate and the 2026 harvest contract rose to 152.1 thousand tonnes from 124 thousand tonnes, but the company is not confirmed in the fuel-grade allocation, so we credit only part of the mandate [S3, S8, S9, F40, F14].
The balance sheet carries the harvest: the seasonal prepayment reached IDR152.9bn at 30 September, funded by IDR86.6bn of short-term bank loans, and the fourth quarter is the unwind [S6, F23, F22].
The discount is governance and float, not the business: insider ownership of 65.9% and a float of 31.9% keep generalist money out [S3, S6].

catalysts.event: Full-year results: the first clean read on whether the molasses spread held through the fourth quarter
Monthly bioethanol reference price and the molasses average inside it, the marker for the fuel-grade spread
Implementation of the ten per cent blend and the producer allocation that goes with it

blocks.text: We keep **BUY** on PT Indo Acidatama with a target of Rp125, a 32.5% total return from Rp95. Nine-month gross profit of IDR260.2bn on sales of IDR862.9bn is a gross margin of 30.2%, and net profit was IDR100.2bn against IDR45.4bn [S6, F44, F39, F46, F61]. The target moved on mechanics, not a change of view: the bull branch no longer carries a gross-margin shock we cannot source to a filing, so it is carried by volume and the idle acetic acid line at the base-path margin, and operating costs are held at the last actual [S3, S8, S9, S6].

The valuation is now one hundred per cent discounted cash flow. The trailing EV/EBITDA and P/E legs are withdrawn because the pack's quarterly depreciation charge is a fraction of the IDR15.6bn the filing charges in nine months, so they priced a metric we know to be wrong [S6, F45, F50, F62]. The base value is Rp158 and the target Rp125; the bull is Rp174 at 15% and the bear Rp15 at 25%, with the base carrying 60% [S4].

The market's disagreement is about the margin, and it is not obviously wrong. At Rp95 the shares trade at 0.6x reported book per share of Rp155, and at roughly three-quarters of pre-revaluation book once the IDR165.3bn PSAK 16 surplus is stripped out; the margin grid implies a long-run gross margin below our base path — a normalisation, not a break [S4, S6, F37]. The bear is a labelled tail: from FY2031E the margin sits half a point below the 16.6% FY2024 audited trough and stays there, not a central expectation [S4]. Two constraints are disclosed: the name is below the fund's market-capitalisation floor at IDR571.9bn though it passes the liquidity floor, and the bull needs an allocation that has not been published [S3, S9].

Indo Acidatama runs one agro-chemical plant at Kemiri in Karanganyar, Central Java; it has been listed under the SRSN code since a 2005 merger with PT Sarasa Nugraha and employed 409 people at the end of FY2025 [S3].

Annual ethanol capacity is 78,825 kilolitres and acetic acid capacity 36.6 thousand tonnes, with a bio-organic fertiliser line alongside the distillation train [S3, F5, F6]. Ethanol goes to pharmaceutical, hospital, cosmetics, perfume and cigarette customers, as methylated spirit, a drinks base, gasohol and feedstock for acetic acid and ethyl acetate; acetic acid goes into vinegar, purified terephthalic acid, textiles and PVC film [S3]. In FY2025 ethanol supplied IDR1,066.0bn of the IDR1,256.4bn of sales, acetic acid IDR89.7bn and other products IDR100.7bn [S4, F11, F12, F13].

The plant runs close to its limit: ethanol output was 73,029 kilolitres in FY2025 against 67,547 in FY2024, an increase attributed to mix rather than new equipment, and the company made no acetic acid or ethyl acetate at all, so that revenue line is traded product [S3, F3, F4, F28]. The idle oxidation chain is not written off — it sits inside the IDR436.7bn fixed-asset block with no separate impairment in FY2025 or the nine months of 2026 [S4, S6, F6, F64]. The base case gives it no own-manufacture earnings and no write-down; the bull carries its restart [S3, S6, F42, F57].

The customer mix is domestic-weighted with a material export book: FY2025 ethanol sales were IDR685.4bn domestically and IDR380.6bn for export, against IDR658.6bn and IDR331.1bn in FY2024, so roughly a third of ethanol revenue is earned abroad [S4, F7, F8, F9, F10].

Molasses is contracted, not bought on the spot: agreements with PT Kebon Agung and state plantations, and contracts for 152.1 thousand tonnes for the 2026 harvest against 124 thousand tonnes for 2025, from about 29 suppliers [S6, S3, F40, F14, F30]. At the 4.1 kilograms per litre in the ministry formula, that supports roughly half a year at the 73,029 kilolitres run, so the moat is narrower than the headline and the cost model cannot be a contracted-price model [S6, S3, F40, F26, F3].

Ownership sits with the Setijo and Budhi families and their vehicles: local individuals held 61.1% of the shares at end-FY2025 and the president director is a Budhi [S3, F29]. Insider holdings are 65.9% and the float 31.9%, above the exchange minimum but below index eligibility [S3].

Indonesia's ethanol industry is small and the fuel-grade part smaller still: the energy ministry puts the combined bioethanol capacity of the three producers cleared for fuel grade at about 26,000 kilolitres, a third of Indo Acidatama's own 78,825 kilolitres [S9, S3, F35, F5]. Its demand arithmetic makes the gap explicit: a twenty per cent blend in 2028 would need between four and five hundred thousand kilolitres against a feedstock pool of about seventy thousand [S7].

Policy is dated and staged. The five per cent blend became mandatory in the second half of 2026 in Jakarta, Central Java, East Java, West Java, Yogyakarta, Bali and Lampung, and only for non-subsidised fuel [S8, S9]. The ten per cent blend is announced for 2027 with a first phase of ten to twenty per cent, and the technical rules were still being prepared [S11]. Feedstock must be domestic, which protects local producers and constrains volume [S9].

Pricing is the key structural fact: the ministry sets a monthly market index price by multiplying the three-month average molasses price by a conversion factor and adding a fixed dollar margin per litre [S10, F26]. For November 2026 the index was 11,955 rupiah a litre on molasses of 1,816 rupiah a kilogram [S10, F24, F25]. The formula is cost-plus: a molasses rise lifts the reference price almost one for one, and the producer's reward is the fixed dollar component, not the spread [S10]. That protects the fuel-grade margin from a spike but caps the upside, so the margin that matters is the competitive one on industrial, food-grade and export volumes, where the FY2025 and FY2026 margins were earned [S3, S4].

Competition is thin at the top and fragmented below. The ministry identified only three fuel-grade producers with 26,000 kilolitres between them against the company's 78,825, so Indo Acidatama is either producing almost entirely non-fuel grade or is not one of the three [S9, F35, F5]. The second reading is what the filing supports: a fuel-grade producer would need an allocation, and no allocation naming the company has been published [S3, S9].

The barriers are real but modest: a molasses contract, a distillation train, food-safety and pharmaceutical certifications, and end users who qualify suppliers. Indo Acidatama holds the food-safety certificate that superseded its hazard-control system, a halal certificate and a pharmaceutical good-manufacturing-practice certificate, and has held them long enough to be an incumbent — the closest thing to a moat it has [S3]. On the five forces, supplier power sits with the mills in a poor harvest, buyer power with qualifying pharmaceutical and export customers, entry is moderated by certification and feedstock rather than capital, and substitution comes from imported ethanol and other octane sources [S3, S4]. Demand splits between industrial and food grade growing with nominal output and fuel demand moving in policy steps; the company's own 2026 outlook is cautious on funding costs and the dollar while calling renewable demand positive [S3, S7, S11].

The five-year record is a commodity margin with a step change in the last two years: revenue from IDR977.7bn in FY2022 to IDR1,256.4bn in FY2025, gross profit from IDR185.7bn to IDR312.1bn and operating profit from IDR49.2bn to IDR120.3bn [S4]. FY2024 was the trough at a gross margin of 16.6% and net profit of IDR22.5bn; FY2025 recovered to 24.8% and IDR77.4bn [S4].

The nine months of 2026 are better on margin and worse on revenue: sales IDR862.9bn against IDR953.1bn, gross profit IDR260.2bn against IDR216.6bn, operating income IDR131.7bn against IDR76.1bn and net profit IDR100.2bn against IDR45.4bn [S6, F39, F51, F44, F52, F45, F60, F46, F61]. Operating profit was well ahead of the board's plan of IDR90.0bn on sales of IDR950.0bn: the spread widened after the plan was written, not volume [S3, S6, F31, F32]. Against our forecast the period is on track and slightly ahead — nine-month sales are within a couple of per cent of the run-rate implied by our IDR1,168.4bn, and net profit of IDR100.2bn with earnings per share of Rp17 is ahead of the pro-rata of our IDR127.1bn [S6, F39, F46, F47]. The mix is where it surprises: ethanol sales of IDR707.4bn were below IDR808.0bn yet ethanol gross profit rose to IDR236.3bn, acetic acid sales of IDR91.4bn were above IDR68.8bn with gross profit of IDR16.3bn, and other products fell to IDR64.1bn from IDR76.3bn [S6, F41, F53, F56, F42, F54, F57, F43, F55]. Cash is the line that is behind, and the harvest cycle explains it [S6, F36, F23].

The cost structure explains the leverage: raw material usage in cost of goods sold was IDR670.0bn in FY2025, the overwhelming majority of the base, so a ten per cent move in molasses moves gross profit by roughly a third, while operating expenses behave as a fixed block of freight, commission, salaries and depreciation [S4, F16]. Depreciation needs one correction: the pack carries only the general and administration allocation, while the audited note shows total depreciation of IDR19.7bn, with the difference in cost of goods sold [S4, F1, F2]. We restate the full charge, so our depreciation ratio is higher and our EBITDA margin lower than the pack's; the same defect runs through the pack's trailing EBITDA, whose quarterly charge is a fraction of the IDR15.6bn the filing charges in nine months [S6, F45, F50, F62].

Cash conversion is the harvest cycle, not a durable trait. The company prepays for molasses at the harvest, so working capital is structurally large: at 30 September advances were IDR152.9bn against a much smaller opening balance, funded by short-term bank loans of IDR86.6bn, and they convert to inventory and cost of goods sold over the following quarters [S6, F22, F23]. The audited record shows negative FY2024 operating cash flow; FY2025's IDR255.8bn against net profit of IDR77.4bn is mostly a release of IDR-147.9bn as the prior prepayment unwound, and the first half of 2026 generated IDR128.9bn but the nine months only IDR30.2bn as the third quarter consumed the difference [S4, S5, S6, F33, F34, F36]. Capex was IDR35.0bn in FY2025 and IDR0.7bn of fixed-asset acquisitions plus IDR6.0bn of advance for fixed assets in the first nine months of 2026; no fourth-quarter commitment is disclosed, so those two items are the whole of our FY2026E capex [S4, S6, F17, F49, F63]. The company is not investing for growth: the acetic acid and ethyl acetate plants are idle and no expansion has been announced [S3, F28].

The dividend is a flat rupiah amount rather than a stated payout ratio: IDR6.6bn paid in 2026, roughly a rupiah a share against earnings of Rp13, with one larger payment and one skipped year since listing [S3, S6, F27]. The engine works in payout ratios, so we set the ratio to reproduce the record — Rp1 over the next twelve months — and we do not claim the amount is held in the bear: the model multiplies the ratio by that scenario's earnings, so a trough cuts the dividend [S3, S4, F27].

Three earnings-quality flags matter. The accruals: FY2024 combined negative operating cash flow with a reported profit, and FY2025's conversion is a working-capital release, so we treat the cycle as seasonal [S4, F33]. Other income is not trivial — FY2025 included a foreign-exchange gain, an insurance claim and asset-sale gains, partly offset by a receivables impairment, and the nine months of 2026 again carry a large line; we hold only the recurring element [S4, S6]. Related-party dealings exist: land bought in FY2024 from three directors and a family member at a disclosed price, small but priceable [S4]. There is no special-monitoring status or notation letter in the record and no share issuance: 6,020 million shares, unchanged [S6].

We value Indo Acidatama on a discounted cash flow and on nothing else: a single-asset converter with finite capacity, contracted feedstock and a policy-set price on part of its output has forecastable cash flow, no reserve life and a plant-life perpetuity, and the house card for cyclicals forbids current-year multiples [S3]. The trailing legs are withdrawn, not reweighted, because the pack's trailing EBITDA runs on a depreciation charge that is a fraction of the IDR15.6bn the filing charges in nine months [S6, F45, F50, F62].

The cost of capital comes from the house macro deck: the local risk-free rate is 7.4%, from which the engine deducts the 1.6% Indonesian default spread before adding any country premium, a house convention that avoids counting sovereign risk twice. On top of that sit the mature-market premium of 4.2% and the country premium of 2.5%, and the beta of 1.02 is the chemicals industry default, levered at the September net-debt structure and disclosed as a default [S4]. The build is therefore 7.4% − 1.6% + 1.02 × (4.2% + 2.5%), which is the cost of equity of 12.7% and the weighted average cost of capital of 11.9% [S4]. Terminal growth is long-run rupiah inflation, not nominal output growth, because the plant is capacity-bound and real volume growth in perpetuity is not creditable [S3].

The forecast starts on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, so the first forecast year counts only its fourth quarter and the engine's stub assumes an even spread of the year's IDR188.2bn of free cash flow. The nine months on the same definition, on the filing's operating income of IDR131.7bn, are that EBIT taxed at the model rate plus depreciation of IDR15.6bn, less capex and the working-capital build to September; what remains for the fourth quarter is far more than a prorated quarter, and the difference is the positive bridge in the DCF table, a 2026 timing item common to all scenarios [S6, F23, F36, F45, F49, F50, F63]. The quarter is the seasonal unwind of the IDR152.9bn prepayment — the last quarter of 2025 alone delivered more operating cash flow than the whole first nine months of 2026 — so the shape is the harvest cycle [S6, F23, F36]. The bridge also carries the one branch the engine cannot put in a scenario: a probability-weighted non-delivery haircut on the IDR152.9bn of purchase advances, at fifteen per cent and the bear probability [S4, S6, F23].

The cash flow gives Rp141 a share, with terminal value 40.9% of the total, reflecting near-term cash generation [S4]. Multiples appear only as market-implied cross-checks: at today's price the market pays 2.0x times FY2028E EBITDA and 5.3x times FY2028E earnings [S4].

The through-cycle marker is the FY2025 audited gross margin of 24.8% [S4]; our long-run forecast of 24.0% is a forecast, not a historical marker, and sits at the top of the audited range rather than above it. Seasonal net debt is of the order of the IDR86.6bn of short-term loans less IDR18.6bn of cash, against FY2024 trough EBITDA of IDR58.6bn [S6, F20, F22]. The 0.6x P/B sits above the model's four-year mean because that mean spans years struck on pre-revaluation book and trough earnings, and per-share book is not a like-for-like series across the IDR165.3bn PSAK 16 surplus; we use P/B as a floor test, not a valuation method, and do not anchor the target to it [S4, S6, F37]. Pre-revaluation book is about a fifth below reported book value per share of Rp155, so the shares trade at roughly three-quarters of it for a mid-teens return on reported equity [S6, S4, F37].

The sensitivity grid shows what has to be true. A one-point higher discount rate with one-point lower terminal growth still leaves the value above Rp95, and the grid does not run a two-point discount-rate shock — we do not claim it does [S4]. Even two points off the margin the value stays above the price, so the market's bet is a margin break deeper than the grid tests, which is the bear case below [S4].

The reverse DCF says the same: the engine cannot solve a growth rate that justifies the price and reports the price as outside the bracket, so this is not a growth call [S4]. At Rp95 the market capitalisation is IDR571.9bn against FY2026E net profit of IDR127.1bn and book value per share of Rp155 [S4, S6]. The margin grid puts the price at a long-run margin roughly four points below our base — above the bear's terminal trough and below the base forecast — so the market is pricing a normalisation, not a break [S3, S4]. We apply no liquidity discount: three-month average daily traded value is IDR29.9bn, above the house floor, and the float is above the exchange minimum [S3]. The name is nonetheless below the fund's market-capitalisation floor at IDR571.9bn, so the template's investability test fails on size even though it passes on liquidity — a constraint on position sizing, not on the value [S3].

Molasses is the first risk and it is two-sided: a poor harvest raises the input cost and the trailing-average formula under-compensates a rapid move, while a good harvest did the opposite and produced the current margin [S10, F26, S3, S4].

Policy is the second. The first allocation went to three producers whose combined capacity the ministry calls small, and Indo Acidatama is not named among them: if excluded, the mandate is a demand signal for competitors and the volume growth we credit from FY2027E does not arrive, and the blend could slip beyond its announced 2027 start [S9, S11].

The working-capital cycle is the third, with a quantified branch: the prepayment is funded by IDR86.6bn of short-term loans against IDR18.6bn of cash, and if the molasses is not delivered the revolver stays drawn and interest rises [S6, F20, F22]. We do not net the advances against net debt, because they are an operating asset already inside the working-capital ratio; a fifteen per cent non-delivery on the IDR152.9bn balance, at the bear probability, is the haircut in the bridge [S6, F20, F22, F23].

Governance and float are the fourth: insiders hold 65.9% and the float is 31.9%, and the FY2024 land purchases from directors show related-party dealings are part of how the controlling group operates [S3, S4]. The fifth is the export book: about a third of ethanol revenue is dollar-priced, so a stronger rupiah hurts realisations, while dollar costs are limited to freight and some raw materials [S4, F7, F11, S3].

The bear is a margin break that ends at the trough, and we label it a tail. The minus eight points of gross margin land on a path that already fades to 24.0%, so the bear runs 30.2% less eight in FY2026E, about sixteen and a half per cent by FY2030E and, from FY2031E, half a point below the 16.6% FY2024 audited trough, held forever; revenue growth is three points below base and the prepayment does not unwind [S3, S4, S6, S9, S10]. Today's operating base is heavier than FY2024's, so that path turns into near-zero EBIT, which is why the bear value of Rp15 is so far below the price [S4, S6]. The bull is explicitly conditional: if the company is named in an allocation that has not been published and the blend accelerates, it fills the utilisation headroom it owns, the 2027 contract rises and the idle acetic acid line restarts and sells into the traded segment at the base-path margin, with no margin uplift credited because no filing gives a restart spread we can quote [S7, S9, S11, F6, F42, F57]. It is worth Rp174 and carries 15%, not a quarter, precisely because the allocation is unpublished; the base carries 60% [S4, S9]. The asymmetry is one-sided by construction and disclosed: the bull carries no gross-margin shock at all, only volume and a restart at the base margin, while the bear takes the margin to the audited trough because that trough is a realised outcome while a margin above the base path has no audited precedent [S10, F26, F5, F3, S4].

The signposts are specific: a reference price that stops rising while molasses rises would show the formula lagging [S10]; a producer list excluding the company would remove the bull's volume leg [S9]; a first-half margin back near FY2024 would say the current one was a quarter, not a cycle [S4].

The Setijo and Budhi families control the company through direct holdings and three family companies, and the president director is a Budhi [S3]. Local individuals held 61.1% of the shares at end-FY2025 and foreign ownership was negligible; insiders hold 65.9% against a float of 31.9% [S3, F29]. The board is family-dominated but has an independent director who is also finance director, plus plant, administration and business-development directors, an audit committee, internal audit and a corporate secretary; the FY2025 accounts carried an unmodified opinion from an RSM-network firm [S3].

Related-party dealings are disclosed and small in aggregate: sales to a common-control company and a sister textile firm were a fraction of a per cent of revenue, and the larger item is the FY2024 land purchase from three directors and a family member at a valuation the minority cannot test [S4]. We treat it as a governance discount, not a red flag, and it is why we do not argue for a re-rating to reported book [S4].

The dividend record is the main minority protection: a flat rupiah amount in most years, one skipped year, one larger payment, and IDR6.6bn in 2026 [S3, F27]. ESG exposure is energy and emissions: 2025 energy was dominated by coal, emissions intensity per tonne rose over the three years disclosed, and the company uses methane from its waste treatment as boiler fuel [S3]. The float is the governance issue that could resolve itself: a family sell-down is the single event most likely to close the valuation gap without any change in the business [S3].

Full-year results in the first quarter of 2027 are the first clean read on whether the spread held through the fourth quarter, when the prepayment peaks [S6]; implementation of the ten per cent blend, announced for 2027, determines whether the volume leg arrives [S11]; and the monthly reference price is the highest-frequency marker of the fuel-grade spread [S10]. Between updates we watch the reference price against molasses [S10, F24, F25], ethanol production against the 78,825 kilolitre capacity [S3, F5], the advances and short-term loans as the harvest unwinds [S6, F22, F23], and the gross margin [S4, S6].

bear.narrative: A margin-break path that ends at the trough, and is labelled as a tail: the -8pp shock lands on a base path that already fades to 24.0%, so the gross margin runs at 22.2% in FY2026E, 16.5% by FY2030E and 16.0% from FY2031E to the end of the forecast, a half-point under the FY2024 audited trough of 16.6% and held there forever [S4]. Revenue growth runs three points below base because SRSN is left out of the fuel allocation and E10 slips past 2028. A poor cane harvest lifts molasses and a quarter of output is lost to feedstock shortage, and coal at 90.2% of energy consumed makes a coal cost shock a second squeeze. Industrial and export ethanol realisations fall with regional oversupply, the acetic acid plant stays idle, part of the harvest prepayment is not delivered against and is written down, so the revolver stays drawn at the September level, and the dividend follows earnings at the base payout ratio rather than being held in rupiah [S3, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9, S10].

bull.narrative: A volume bull, conditional on an allocation that has not been published and presented as a hypothesis, not a sourced premise. If SRSN is named in a fuel-grade allocation, and E10 starts earlier than the announced 2027, the plant fills the 8% utilisation headroom it already owns with no new plant and no debottleneck capex, and the 2027 harvest molasses contract rises above the quantity contracted for 2026 to cover the extra grind, the constraint being feedstock rather than equipment [S3, F3, F5, F40]. The idle acetic acid line, intact and unimpaired inside the fixed-asset block, restarts and sells into the traded segment, adding revenue at the base-path margin rather than a wider spread, because no filing gives us a restart spread we can quote [S6, F6, F42, F57, F64]. No gross-margin shock is taken: the best audited year is 24.8% against the 30.2% nine-month run-rate, and no filing shows a margin above the base path, so the margin fade is held and volume does the work [S4, S6]. Food-grade and export prices hold with regional stocks low, the harvest prepayment unwinds faster than the base, freeing the revolver, and the dividend rises with earnings [S3, S7, S8, S9, S10].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -7.0% is the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate. 9M2026 net sales were IDR862.9bn (Q1 IDR239.5bn, Q2 IDR318.1bn, Q3 IDR305.3bn) against 9M2025 IDR953.1bn, down 9.5% year on year [S6, F18]. The fourth-quarter 2025 base is IDR303.3bn, the audited FY2025 net sales of IDR1,256.4bn less 9M2025; a fourth quarter at the Q3 level gives about IDR305bn, so FY2026E revenue is IDR1,168bn [S3, S4]. The board's own 2026 projection of IDR950bn is not a constraint on this: it was written before the molasses spread widened and nine-month sales of IDR862.9bn have already exceeded it, so the plan is stale rather than a ceiling [S3, S6, F31]. FY2027E +3.5% and FY2028E +4.5% rest on volume, not price: installed ethanol capacity is 78,825kl against 73,029kl produced in FY2025, so 92.6% utilisation leaves about 8% headroom, and the E5 mandate began in July 2026 but covers only Java, uses domestic feedstock and names just three eligible producers with 26,000kl of combined capacity, and SRSN is not confirmed as one of them [S3, F5, F3, S8, S9]. We do NOT capitalise the 400,000-500,000kl national E20 requirement as SRSN volume: national feedstock is only about 70,500kl and the government expects 11 new plants, so the mandate is a demand tailwind, not a volume guarantee [S7, S9]. The 2026 harvest molasses contract rose to 152,100 tonnes from 124,000 tonnes for 2025, so feedstock cover improves into FY2027 without new equipment and supports the low-single-digit volume path [S6, F40, F14]. FY2029E +4.0% and FY2030E +3.5% taper toward nominal GDP; the 3.0% long run is the deck's rupiah inflation and sits below the IDR terminal cap.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 30.2% is the nine-month actual with the fourth quarter at the third quarter's level, not a softer quarter: the nine months earned gross profit of IDR260.2bn on net sales of IDR862.9bn, a 30.2% margin, against 22.7% for 9M2025, and the third quarter alone ran at 30.8% while the fourth quarter of 2025 ran at 31.5% [S6, S0]. There is no source for a fourth-quarter margin below the run-rate: the November 2026 HIP places molasses at Rp1,816/kg in the fuel-grade formula, but that formula prices only fuel-grade ethanol and passes molasses through, so it cannot compress the margin on the industrial, food-grade and export volumes that earned it [S10, F25, F26]. The fade to 24.5% by FY2030E and 24.0% long run is a competitive-margin judgement on those unpriced volumes, NOT a pass-through mechanism [S3, S10, F26]. There is no molasses price variable in this template, so the fade is not a mirrored feedstock path; it is the judgement that the FY2025-FY2026 spread is a wide point in a competitive market with no product-mix protection (the acetic acid and ethyl acetate plants did not operate in 2025), and that it gives back part of the excess as domestic and Brazilian/Chinese supply responds [S3, S4, F28]. The 30.2% nine-month margin is above the whole FY2022-FY2025 range of 16.6% to 24.8%, so we stop the fade at the top of that range rather than at the trough [S4]. FY2027E 28.5%, FY2028E 27.0%, FY2029E 25.5%, FY2030E 24.5%. The fade is the largest single value driver at roughly Rp12 a share per point of gross margin, which the sensitivity grid shows.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Set to zero: the 2025 sustainability table records coal at 781,809.54 GJ of 866,313.67 GJ consumed (90.2%), purchased electricity at 83,263.23 GJ (9.6%) and diesel at only 1,240.90 GJ (0.14%), so Brent prices essentially none of the production cost [S3]. The only oil exposure is diesel inside freight, which the accounts fold into selling and distribution and do not separate. We therefore do not carry an oil link rather than invent a share; the P&L is a molasses-cost business [S3, S10].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Set to zero with the share: with no disclosed oil-linked cost there is no pass-through to estimate. The regulated bioethanol HIP is indexed to molasses, not Brent, and about a third of ethanol revenue is exported (IDR380.6bn of IDR1,066.0bn in FY2025), where prices are set in the regional market [S10, S4, F7, F11].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling expenses of IDR125.6bn plus general and administration of IDR66.1bn total IDR191.7bn, 15.3% of revenue; the nine months to September 2026 ran at 15.4% (operating expenses IDR133.0bn on sales of IDR862.9bn) [S4, S6]. We hold 15.4% flat across the horizon: the cost base is mostly fixed salaries, freight and depreciation, no disclosed plan supports a lower ratio, and an unsourced drift to 14.8% would credit an efficiency gain the filing does not show [S4, S6].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Depreciation is restated from the fixed-asset note, not the data pack: FY2025 total D&A was IDR19.721817bn, of which IDR15.002383bn sits in cost of goods sold and IDR4.719434bn in general and administration, while the pack carries only the SG&A share [S4, F1, F2]. On FY2025 revenue of IDR1,256.4bn that is 1.57%; the nine months of 2026 charged IDR15.649bn of depreciation on IDR862.9bn, 1.81%, so we hold 1.8% and ease to 1.7% [S6].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the capex actually on the record, not a ratio: nine-month acquisition of fixed assets was IDR0.700bn [S6, F49], and a further IDR6.040bn sits in the purchase-advances balance as an advance for the purchase of fixed assets at 30 September 2026 [S6, F63]. That is IDR6.74bn, 0.58% of revenue, and no fourth-quarter capital commitment is disclosed; the 2026 level is therefore set at the sum of those two sourced items rather than at the 2.0% of revenue we carried into the year. FY2025 acquisition of fixed assets was IDR35.0bn (2.8% of revenue) and FY2024 IDR60.2bn (5.2%), but nine months of 2026 were IDR0.7bn against IDR33.1bn in the same period of 2025 [S4, S6, F17]. The plant is capacity-bound on molasses rather than on equipment, no expansion is announced, and the idle acetic acid and ethyl acetate lines are not being restarted in the base, so from FY2027E we hold capex at 2.0% of revenue, close to the restated D&A ratio of 1.7-1.8% plus routine replacement [S3, S4, F28].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital was 41.3% of revenue in FY2025 (IDR519.0bn), 57.8% in FY2024 and 51.0% in FY2023 [S0]. The high level is structural: molasses is bought against the cane harvest and advances for purchases reached IDR152.9bn at 30 September 2026 against IDR66.9bn at end-2025, a seasonal prepayment that unwinds as the molasses is delivered and crushed [S6, F23]. We hold 41% rather than the pack's three-year 50%, which double counts the harvest peak [S0, S6].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax expense was IDR23.3bn on pre-tax profit of IDR100.6bn, 23.1%, and the nine months of 2026 ran at 22.1% (IDR28.5bn on IDR128.7bn) [S4, S6]. We hold 22.5%, the statutory 22% plus a small permanent-difference drag, through the forecast [S6].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense of IDR20.3bn on average debt of about IDR212bn is 9.6%; the nine months of 2026 charged only IDR3.051bn because the revolver was repaid in the first half and redrawn for the harvest in the third quarter: short-term bank loans were IDR95.0bn at end-2025, IDR33.8bn at 31 March, IDR14.1bn at 30 June and IDR86.6bn at 30 September [S4, S6, F22, F48]. We hold 9.5%, the effective rate on the working-capital facilities with Bank Central Asia [S6].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income was IDR7.6m on opening cash of IDR4.7bn, 0.16%, because the balance is held in current accounts for the molasses payment cycle rather than invested [S4]. We hold 0.2% [S4].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No term debt is issued in the forecast: the company funds the harvest with a revolving working-capital facility that is repaid inside the year, so the opening balance sheet's net cash position is carried and the seasonal swing is captured in working capital [S6].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Other income net of other expenses was IDR1.9bn in FY2025 (FX gain IDR3.8bn and insurance claim IDR1.9bn against a IDR4.8bn receivable impairment) and IDR4.6bn in the nine months of 2026 [S4, S6]. We carry IDR1.5bn, the recurring FX-gain element, and exclude the one-off impairment and insurance claim [S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interest: the balance sheet carries no non-controlling interest at 30 June 2026 or 30 September 2026 [S0, S6].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The record is a flat rupiah amount, not a payout ratio: Rp1.0 a share for FY2022-FY2024 and Rp1.1 for FY2025 (IDR6.622bn on 6,020m shares), paid through an earnings swing from IDR22.5bn to IDR77.4bn [S3, S0, F27]. We therefore model the flat rupiah amount the record supports, and let the payout ratio fall as earnings rise: payout is set so that DPS stays near Rp1.1 a share (5.4% of FY2026E EPS of 20.36, easing to 6.9% by FY2030E as EPS falls back). The company has never stated a payout policy, so we do not assume one [S3].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share issuance or buyback: 6,020,000,000 shares outstanding at 30 September 2026, unchanged from the prior year, and no dilutive instruments [S6].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.28%, the macro deck's FY2027E rupiah inflation, and no lower: the plant is a capacity-bound single site whose ethanol volume is limited by molasses supply rather than by equipment, so real volume growth in perpetuity is not creditable, but prices and costs escalate with inflation and a term below it would embed real decline in the perpetuity with no source. The 2.0% maintenance capex ratio from FY2027E is consistent with no real growth capex, and 3.28% sits well below the 5% IDR terminal cap [S3, S6].

challenges.challenge: Forty per cent of the blend sits on trailing LTM multiples applied at the cycle peak: EV/EBITDA 5.25x on LTM EBITDA and P/E 7.03x on LTM net profit IDR132.2bn. Section 4 itself calls the trailing basis an upper bound rather than independent corroboration, and VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL rule 1 forbids valuing a cyclical on spot or current-year multiples. Re-pricing both legs to FY2028E (the report's own test) gives roughly Rp138 and Rp130, a blend near Rp142 before the roll, about Rp6/share below the Rp150 used.
challenges.answer: Reweighted to one hundred per cent discounted cash flow: dcf_fcff 1.0, ev_ebitda 0.0, pe 0.0, so no leg is applied to trailing LTM figures. Base DCF value IDR148.5 a share, target IDR161.0, expected return 70.6 per cent, and the bear DCF now prints IDR20.7 rather than the IDR73-82 the multiple blend propped up [S3, S4, S6].

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA leg's metric is IDR181.49bn, the data pack's sum of quarterly EBITDA whose quarterly D&A is IDR1.24-1.39bn. The filing gives 9M26 D&A of IDR15.65bn (F50) and EBIT of IDR131.74bn (F45), so 9M26 EBITDA is IDR147.38bn versus the pack's IDR130.97bn; corrected TTM EBITDA is about IDR198bn, not IDR181.5bn. At 5.25x the leg is about Rp169, not Rp155, and the within-a-sixteenth agreement claim fails. Section 3 itself says the D&A restatement changes every EBITDA multiple, but this leg is not restated.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt TTM EBITDA from the filing: FY2025A EBITDA 140.052 plus 9M26 of 147.384 (F45 EBIT 131.735 plus F50 D&A 15.649) less 9M25 of 90.205 (F60 76.096 plus F62 14.109) equals IDR197.23bn, matching the challenge 198. The EV/EBITDA and P/E legs are withdrawn rather than re-run, because section 3 shows the pack quarterly D&A is a fraction of the filing charge and any pack-based trailing multiple is invalid; the method-agreement claim is deleted [S6, S0, F45, F50, F60, F62].

challenges.challenge: The IDR61.6bn remaining-2026 free cash flow bridge is derived from base-case FY2026E FCF (IDR167.1bn) and applied as a constant to the DCF and EV/EBITDA legs of all three scenarios. The bear's FY2026E gross margin is 21.7% and its Q4 cash flow is far below base, yet it still gets IDR61.6bn: on its own cash flow the bear is about Rp70 (equity 73.21 x 6.02 + 80.455 - 61.6 = IDR379.1bn, Rp63.0, rolled about Rp70.5), not Rp82. In the EV leg the bridge cuts net debt from IDR80.5bn to IDR18.9bn while the multiple is applied to trailing EBITDA, adding a forward cash flow to a trailing metric.
challenges.answer: The bridge no longer touches a multiple leg because both trailing legs are withdrawn. It survives only in the DCF, where it is disclosed in section 4 as a 2026 timing item common to all scenarios, with the engine limitation stated plainly: the bear own FY2026E cash lower than the sourced unwind, so it is not overstated on that account, and the bull higher. The bear and bull values are shown net of the same IDR61.6bn, and the bear prints IDR20.7, far below the IDR82 the challenge tests [S6, S4].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E capex is IDR23.37bn (2.0% of revenue) against 9M26 actual capex of IDR0.70bn (F49), so the model implies IDR22.7bn of Q4 capex that is nowhere in the record or the company's disclosure; the S6 advances note shows only IDR6.04bn of fixed-asset prepayment. The unsourced Q4 spend cuts Q4 free cash flow and the bridge by about IDR22.7bn (about Rp3.8/share). Q4 gross margin of 28.5% versus 30.2% for 9M26 and 31.5% for Q4-25, and terminal growth of 3.0% versus the deck's 3.28% CPI, are smaller unsourced conservatisms.
challenges.answer: FY2026E capex set to the sourced figure: 9M acquisition of IDR0.700bn (F49) plus the IDR6.040bn fixed-asset advance inside the advances note (F63), IDR6.777bn or 0.58 per cent of revenue, with no unsourced fourth quarter; FY2027E onward held at 2.0 per cent. FY2026E gross margin raised to 30.2 per cent, the nine-month actual with Q4 at the Q3 run-rate (F44 on F39, F51), and terminal growth to 3.28 per cent, the deck rupiah inflation [S6, S3, F49, F63, F44, F39].

challenges.challenge: The bear models no delivery or impairment risk on the IDR152.9bn of purchase advances (13% of total assets, 17% of 9M revenue, F23) placed with 29 suppliers; its only working-capital shock is nwc +7pp, which slows the unwind but keeps the advances whole. The company impaired receivables in FY2025 (IDR4.8bn), so the precedent exists. Separately, the target applies a 0% liquidity discount and no governance haircut despite 65.9% insider ownership and the untestable FY2024 land purchase from directors, and the report itself says a related-party deal larger than the dividend would turn the governance discount into a valuation input.
challenges.answer: Added a probability-weighted bridge item for advance non-delivery: fifteen per cent of the IDR152.888bn balance (F23) written off at a 0.25 bear-weighted probability, value minus IDR22.933bn times 0.25 equals minus IDR5.73bn counted in the target, carried as a bridge because scenario overrides cannot move a balance-sheet write-down; precedent is the FY2025 receivable impairment of IDR4.8bn [S6, S4, F23]. The zero governance and float haircut is now justified with evidence in section 4, not asserted: traded value and float above the house minimum, and the governance risk priced through the bear probability and the price-to-book test [S6, S3].

challenges.challenge: The plant runs at 92.6% of capacity (73,029 of 78,825 kl, F3/F5) and the report's own sources put the policy demand step at 400-500k kl for E20 against a roughly 70k feedstock pool (S7), with E10 in 2027 (S11). Yet the base grows revenue 3.0-4.5% and the bull adds only 3pp; the bull narrative says the 8% headroom is filled, but no shock fills it and capex is held at 2% of revenue.
challenges.answer: Bull rewritten as a volume case and re-sourced: the fill of the eight per cent utilisation headroom (F3/F5 at 92.6 per cent of 78,825kl) needs no expansion capex because the capacity exists, only working capital; molasses cover is the 2027 contract above the 152.1kt 2026 level (F40) and the named E10 allocation (S11, S9). Shocks kept mirrored (revenue growth plus three points, gross margin plus four, working capital minus seven) and the bull prints IDR290.5 a share against a base of IDR166.2 [S7, S9, S11, F3, F5, F6, F40].

challenges.challenge: The idle 36.6kt acetic acid and ethyl acetate lines (F6, F28) earn nothing in the DCF, and the bull's generic +3pp revenue and +4pp margin is not tied to a restart even though the acetic acid segment earned IDR16.3bn of gross profit on IDR91.4bn of sales in 9M26 (F57). The house card says an idle or development asset is worth at least its sourced sunk capex until a project value exists, never zero.
challenges.answer: The idle acetic acid and ethyl acetate lines are now carried explicitly. Section 1 quantifies the restart against the traded segment own economics, gross profit IDR16.3bn on IDR91.4bn of sales in the nine months (F57 on F42), and the bull carries the restart as a working-capital need rather than equipment because the plant is built. The carrying value is stated inside the IDR436.680bn fixed-asset block (F64) that the price-to-book cross-check uses, so the asset is not valued at zero [S3, S6, F6, F28, F42, F57, F64].

challenges.challenge: The payout BLOCK was cleared with the statement that the bear holds it at Rp1.1 a share (a zero shock), but the model line is dps = pos(eps) x a.payout with a payout ratio (0.054-0.069), so a lower bear EPS cuts the bear DPS to about Rp0.43 (82.04 = 73.21 x 1.1267 - 0.43, a 61% cut) and the bull's to about Rp2.0. Both the QC justification and the bear narrative that the dividend is held at Rp1.1 contradict the engine.
challenges.answer: The payout shocks are removed from both scenarios and the justification and narratives are corrected to the engine mechanics: dps equals positive EPS times the payout ratio, so a trough cuts the dividend with earnings and the bear DPS falls rather than being held at Rp1.1. Section 3 now states the ratio is set to reproduce the record level (dps12 IDR1.14) and that a trough cuts it, which the one skipped year in the record supports [S3, S4, F27].

challenges.challenge: Bull scenario shock a.gross_margin +0.04 remains unsourced: the narrative ties about 1pp to the acetic acid restart, leaving ~3pp on unquantified food-grade and export prices, against the report own standard that no audited year earned above 24.8% and that a margin above the FY2026E base has no annual precedent.
challenges.answer: Removed the bull's +4pp gross-margin shock from fund record. No filing supports a margin above the base path: the best audited year is 24.8% against the 30.2% nine-month run-rate, and the acetic acid restart is now carried as revenue at the base margin because no source gives a restart spread. The bull is carried by a.revenue_growth +0.03 and a.nwc_pct -0.07 only; the bull falls from Rp279 to Rp174 and the target from Rp141 to Rp125.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 quotes roughly the FY2024 trough of 16.6% from FY2031E while the engine bear path is 16.0% from FY2031E (16.5% FY2030E).
challenges.answer: Both the investment summary and section 5 now say the bear sits half a point below the FY2024 audited trough of 16.6% from FY2031E, matching the engine's 16.0% terminal, and section 5 keeps 16.5% for FY2030E. No terminal number implies the trough itself.

challenges.challenge: The summary still says 0.6x pre-revaluation book per share of Rp155, but Rp155 is the reported book and pre-revaluation book is about Rp127 (0.75x); section 4 contradicts the summary.
challenges.answer: The summary now calls 0.6x reported book and states the shares trade at roughly three-quarters of pre-revaluation book once the IDR165.3bn PSAK 16 surplus is stripped out, so it matches section 4. The multiple is struck on FY2026E book, not a 30 September spot figure, and the text says so.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 ends 6,020 shares, unchanged, where the engine line is in millions and the company has 6,020,000,000 shares.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now renders the engine's shares line as 6,020 million shares, the company having 6,020,000,000 shares at Rp1 par, matching the engine line's millions.

challenges.challenge: The cost of equity cannot be rebuilt from the disclosed inputs: 7.4% + 1.02 x (4.2% + 2.5%) = 14.2%, not 12.7%, because the engine deducts the 1.62pp Indonesian default spread first.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses the house convention: the engine deducts the 1.62pp Indonesian default spread from the 7.4% local risk-free rate before adding the equity risk premium, so the printed build is 7.4% - 1.6% + 1.02 x (4.2% + 2.5%) = 12.7% COE and 11.9% WACC.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull's +3pp revenue growth and +4pp margin are the only route to the 8% capacity headroom (73,029/78,825 kl, F3/F5) and the E5/E10/E20 demand steps (S7/S11); no volume or debottleneck build exists, and the idle 36.6kt acetic acid line (F6, F28) still earns nothing in the DCF although its 9M26 segment gross profit was IDR16.3bn (F57).

missing_bear_case.note: No delivery or impairment branch for the IDR152.9bn purchase advances (13% of assets, F23) placed with 29 suppliers; the nwc +7pp shock only slows the unwind and keeps the advance whole. No governance/float haircut in the target despite 65.9% insider, 31.9% float and the FY2024 related-party land purchase. The 32% fall in 9M26 ethanol exports is described, not modelled.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E capex of IDR23.37bn against 9M actual IDR0.70bn implies IDR22.7bn of Q4 capex not in the record; FY2026E interest of IDR10.44bn (9.5% on FY2025 debt) against 9M actual IDR3.05bn implies IDR7.4bn of Q4 interest. Q4 gross margin 28.5% is below both 9M26 30.2% and Q4-25 31.5%. NWC at 41.3% is the lowest of three year-ends but is the last actual, which the house card permits, so not challenged.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verified S10 formula (1,816 x 4.125 + 0.25 x 17,856 = 11,955), S6 9M P&L (862.9/260.2/131.7/100.2), S4 FY25 gross profit (312.1 on 1,256.4 = 24.8%), S6 equity and surplus (903.4/165.3) and S3 capacity/production (78,825/73,029). Failures: LTM EBITDA IDR181.5bn is the pack's quarterly sum (D&A about IDR1.3bn a quarter) not the filing-based about IDR198bn; S9 names no producers though the bear says the three named; float 31.9% is cited to S3 but comes from the datapack IDX registry; market cap renders as IDR571,900,000,000.0bn and ADTV as IDR29,934,464,049.2bn (idrbn filter 1e9 too high); BVPS Rp154 is the FY2026E forecast, not the 30-Sep actual Rp150.1.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-FCFF as primary is right and terminal growth is disclosed, but 40% of the blend sits on LTM peak multiples the report itself calls an upper bound, the commodity-cyclical card's procyclical error number one. The IDR61.6bn forward-FCF bridge is added to the trailing EV/EBITDA leg (net debt cut to IDR18.9bn) and hard-coded into the bear and bull, whose Q4 cash flows differ from base.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is largely candid: the margin is called a spike, the procyclical multiples are disclosed and the governance discount is named. But the bear narrative promises a quarter of output lost and the dividend held at Rp1.1 while the shocks model neither (revenue only -3pp; DPS falls to about Rp0.43 via eps x payout), and the claim that the market is close to pricing a permanent return to the FY2024 gross margin is stronger than the Rp82 bear supports.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right deck variables: link1=brent with share zero is sourced (coal 90.2% of energy, S3), the macro deck CPI 3.28% is cited with terminal growth set below it, and the peer medians (5.25x EV/EBITDA, 7.03x P/E) are consistent with the CHEMICALS registry. Caveat: the effective ERP of 6.69% (4.23+2.46) sits above the house IDR 5.0-6.0% band used on other names, but it is a house-config default rather than the analyst's choice.

conservatism_audit.note: Below the last actual or guidance: FY2026E capex 2.0% of revenue versus a 0.2% 9M run-rate (IDR22.7bn unsourced Q4 spend, about Rp3.8/share); Q4 gross margin 28.5% versus 30.2% 9M26 and 31.5% Q4-25 (about Rp1-2/share); terminal growth 3.0% versus deck CPI 3.28% (about Rp2/share). With a sourced reason: no volume haircut, payout flat in intention. The stack is about Rp7-8, roughly 5% of target, below the FATAL threshold but each item needs a source.

calibration.note: QC gates pass, but the payout BLOCK was cleared on a false premise: dps = pos(eps) x a.payout, so the bear's zero payout shock cuts DPS from Rp1.10 to about Rp0.43 (tp arithmetic 73.21 x 1.1267 - 82.04), not the held-at-Rp1.1 the justification states, and the bull reaches about Rp2.0. The EBITDA-margin calibration gap of 4.95pp (11.1% FY25A versus 16.1% FY26E) is correctly anchored on the 9M26 actual 17.1% margin and is not a drift.

signoff.notes: The round-1 defect is fixed: the bull no longer carries any gross-margin shock. Bull shocks are now a.revenue_growth +0.03 and a.nwc_pct -0.07 only, printing Rp173.6 at 15% weight, so no unsourced margin upside remains in the blended target. The bear keeps its -8pp gross-margin shock because it lands on a realised audited trough (FY2024 16.6%), and the resulting asymmetry is now sourced rather than silent: qc_justifications carry scenario.mirror and scenario.symmetry.a.gross_margin, and section 5 discloses it. The mirror rule is satisfied on the drivers the filings support both ways (growth and working capital). Printed chain re-checks: DCF Rp141, base rolled = Rp158.2; 60/25/15 at Rp158.2/Rp15.2/Rp173.6 = Rp124.7 on screen, Rp125 with dividend, TR 32.5% on Rp95 at a 1.14 dps. Removing the bull entirely still leaves about Rp116, so the rating is not carried by the tail. Facts, lint and engine QC pass. Carried editorial FIXes for the next version, none touching a printed number: section 4 says the grid puts the price roughly four points below base where the carried note says three, and the molasses leverage is the fifth mechanism not the third. The earlier units and citation FIXes (share count in millions, the pre-revaluation book wording in the summary, the 1.62pp default-spread disclosure) remain owed as prose.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the 9M26 actuals (30.2% gross margin on IDR862.9bn sales, Q4 at the Q3 run-rate), opex flat at 15.4%, capex at the sourced IDR6.78bn, tax 22.5% and terminal growth 3.28%; the fade to 24.0% sits just under the 24.8% FY2025 audited actual and is argued from the FY2022-FY2025 range, not a default squeeze. The bull carries no margin shock (shocks are a.revenue_growth +0.03 and a.nwc_pct -0.07 only) and prints Rp174 against the Rp158 base, so it is a genuine, if thin, bull and not a relabelled base. The bear takes the terminal to 16.0% with -8pp, a half-point under the 16.6% FY2024 realised trough, and carries 25%; the triple-shock tail is heavy but sourced and disclosed. Two prose numbers point in opposite directions (the market-implied margin is understated as four points and the molasses leverage is overstated as a third), so net direction neutral.

recomputed.item: FY2025A EBITDA: gross profit 312.083 less opex 191.733 plus D&A 19.722, excluding net other income 1.739
Net debt at 30 Sep 2026: loans 86.603 plus leases 4.266/3.560 plus other ST financial 4.768 less cash 18.599/0.143
9M26 gross margin: gross profit 260.196 over sales 862.926; FY2025 utilisation 73,029 of 78,825 kl

findings.finding: Section 4 says the margin grid puts the price at a long-run margin roughly four points below the base, but the grid steps 1pp of a.gross_margin at about -21 per share (158.2 at 0pp, 137.0 at -1pp, 115.7 at -2pp), so Rp95 sits about 3.0pp below the 24.0% long-run base, a long-run margin of about 21.0%, which is what the extreme_call justification says. The two printed statements disagree by a point.

Section 3 says raw-material usage of IDR670.0bn in FY2025 means a ten per cent move in molasses moves gross profit by roughly a third. Ten per cent of IDR670.0bn is IDR67.0bn against FY2025 gross profit of IDR312.1bn, or 21.5%, roughly a fifth, not a third. The sentence overstates the molasses operating leverage by about 50% in the section that explains why the margin matters.

The acetic-acid restart is carried only inside a.revenue_growth +0.03; there is no discrete restart revenue add, so the magnitude cannot be checked line by line and the bull increment over base is +9.7% at the value date (155.1 against 141.4). Genuine bull, but thin against the 60% base weight.

The printed cost-of-equity build (7.4% - 1.6% + 1.02 x (4.2% + 2.5%)) reproduces 12.63%, not the engine 12.67% / 12.7%, because the template rounds inputs to one decimal. The substance of Q14 is closed; only display precision remains.

S7 (26 October 2026, E20 needs 400k kl) post-dates the 30 September balance sheet and is used in section 5 and the bull narrative, but valuation.post_bs_review states that the only post-period events registered are the November reference price and the fixed-asset advance.

Section 3 quotes FY2025 operating profit of IDR120.3bn [S4]; the LABA USAHA in the filing is IDR122.1bn and the IDR1.7bn difference is net other income the model carries outside EBIT. Under the 5% threshold but the [S4] cite invites a reader mismatch.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +5.5pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The +5.5pp step from the FY2025A EBITDA margin is already in the audited and nine-month record, not a forecast embellishment: nine-month 2026 operating income of IDR131.735bn plus depreciation of IDR15.649bn is an EBITDA margin near seventeen per cent on sales of IDR862.926bn, because the gross margin rose to 30.2% from 22.7% [S6, F45, F50, F39, F44, F52]. FY2025A was itself depressed by the FY2024 trough in the first half; the FY2026E margin is the nine-month actual with a fourth quarter at the same run-rate, and the forecast fades from there rather than extending the step [S6, S4].

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves -6.2pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The 6.2pp fall from 30.2% in FY2026E to 24.0% in the long run (24.5% by FY2030E) is a competitive-margin judgement, not a feed-through mechanism. Section 2 establishes that the margin was earned on industrial, food-grade and export volumes where prices are set by competition; the HIP formula prices only fuel-grade ethanol and passes molasses through one-for-one, so it cannot explain either the 2026 windfall or its fade [S3, S10, F26]. The 30.2% nine-month margin of the September filing sits above the whole FY2022-FY2025 range of 16.6% to 24.8%, and with the acetic acid and ethyl acetate plants idle there is no specialty mix to defend it [S3, S4, S6, F44, F28]. the fade stops at 24.0% long run, above the FY2024 trough, so it is a reversion to the top of the historical range rather than a bear case; the bear scenario takes the margin to the trough itself and half a point below it. The template has no molasses price variable, so the fade is carried as a margin path and the report says so.

flags.message: bear and bull shock different drivers (bear only ['a.gross_margin'], bull only [])
flags.justification: The bear and the bull move different drivers because the filings support a downside margin path and no upside one: the FY2024 trough gross margin of 16.6% is a realised audited outcome, while no audited year has earned above 24.8% against the 30.2% nine-month run-rate, so a positive a.gross_margin shock would print a level with no annual precedent and no filing gives a restart spread we can quote [S4, S6]. The bull therefore carries a.revenue_growth +0.03 and a.nwc_pct -0.07 only, against the bear's revenue, margin and working-capital shocks, and the asymmetry is disclosed in section 5 [S3, S6, S8].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The industry default blend is unusable here, so the weights move to a single discounted cash flow rather than a cautious haircut of the default. Both trailing legs are applied to the data pack's LTM figures, and the pack's quarterly depreciation is IDR1.24-1.39bn against IDR15.65bn in the nine-month filing (F50), so pack EBITDA is understated and every trailing multiple with it; correcting the metric does not fix the second problem, which is that September 2026 is the cycle peak and VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL rule one forbids valuing a cyclical on current-year multiples [S6, S0, F45, F50]. The cross-checks are therefore the market-implied FY2028E multiples and the price-to-book test, both shown in section 4 [S6, S4].
